"There's still the matter of the ambush of Wanjiru. Nobody's settled it."

The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Take care out there."
"Can I tell you something? I saw something in the woods I'm not telling anyone about."
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Brian rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Nobody's worked the east treeline in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
Finish the fight before foraging together.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"I dreamed Irving was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I should let you go. Be well, okay?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Are you going to stay? With us. For real."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Good. We're better with you here. I mean that."
"I stay where I'm useful. Right now that's here. Denver is a direction, not a plan. Here is a plan, even if it's a hard one."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"...Still on whether you're staying."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"I asked Keisha about the pantry run — Keisha's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"I still need help with the pantry run."
You need to be right next to your partner, same side of the Haven door, to help.
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"

"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.

They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"

"See you around."

Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.

Ellie looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."

"Still on that personal stuff."
They glance away, then back. Different subject, same worry:
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:

"Can I tell you something? I don't actually know how to swim and I'm terrified someone will find out."

You walk to the tree line with Binsar. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"We went over this," Binsar says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."

"...I need to go be quiet for a while."

"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Me? Odesa, Ukraine. I still dream in its weather — rain on a tin roof, that specific smell. I wake up here and for a second I'm furious at the sky for the swap."
"Still on where you're from."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"The whole fire was arguing about The Landlord last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"We'll land on something. We always do — usually the loudest person's idea."

They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that plant lesson. I'm listening."

"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "I dreamed June was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I check everyone's shoes for wear. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."

"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."

"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I put down The Ugly Bastard at the treeline. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Good. I mean it — watch yourself out there."
"I keep thinking about that Sir Blinds-A-Lot. It knows this ground now. Keep your eyes up past the treeline."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.

A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I'm not from Denver. I'm from Tucson, Arizona. The truth felt small. The lie felt like someone worth keeping around." Quiet. Real.

"If you see that Sir Blinds-A-Lot again, don't try to be clever. Get back inside the palisade."
"Thank you. I needed to hear you say it."
"I don't know what's moving out there, but something is. Keep your eyes up past the treeline."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Pattern Hunger. They just... took Dale. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I should get back to it."

"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"

"...Fine. This had better be worth it."

d15: 🕯️ Irving Maier is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
